newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BONN PLANS GOLD MOVE TO REDUCE ITS DEFICIT

Germany has proposed a revaluation of its gold reserves in a move which has been seen as a creative accounting device to help the country meet the criteria for joining the single European currency. The plans follow the publication of an experts report predicting a DM118 billion (42 billion sterling) shortfall in budgeted revenues between now and 2001.
-- FT-SE PARTNERSHIP LAUNCHES TWO PAN-EUROPEAN INDICES

An international partnership involving FTSE International and Amsterdam's stock and options exchange is to launch a new set of pan-European stock market indices. The move reflects a desire among investors to look at shares on a Europe-wide basis, as the EU moves towards a single market and single currency. The new indices, the FTSE Eurotop 100 and 300, will comprise Europe's largest and most liquid stocks.
-- EARLIER LAUNCH OF EURO URGED

Yves-Thibault de Silguy, the European Union commissioner for monetary affairs, has floated the idea of bringing forward the introduction of euro notes and coins by several months to the autumn of 2001. The proposal is aimed at avoiding the possible mayhem of a January launch coinciding with post-Christmas discount sales.
-- BBC PUSHES AHEAD WITH 24-HOUR DIGITAL CHANNEL

The BBC is to continue with its plans for a 24-hour digital television channel despite the postponement of the launch of digital satellite television. Setting up the channel is costing the BBC 30 million sterling, and it is expected to have annual running costs of 10-12 million sterling. The BBC had planned for the channel to be ready for October, when BSkyB was due to launch 200 channels of digital satellite television, but that launch has now been put back until next spring.
-- SALICK TO COMPETE WITH ZENECA AFTER ABRUPT DEPARTURE

Dr Bernard Salick, who sold his kidney clinics Salick Health Care to UK drugs company Zeneca and then proceeded to quit the company rather than take a demotion from chief executive to chairman emeritus, has announced he was attempting to raise 185 million sterling to compete with Zeneca. Salick has put up between ten and 20 million dollars of his new venture, Bentley Health Care, which would reportedly operate a series of cancer and Aids/HIV clinics and is hoping to raise between 100 and 300 million dollars from outside investors.
-- SCOTTISH POWER LEAPS 38 PERCENT

Glasgow based multi-utility Scottish Power has reported full-year results which show a 38 percent rise in pre-tax profits of 554.4 million sterling to March 31 and overall turnover up 30 percent to 2.94 billion sterling. Scottish Power accompanied the results with an announcement that after the purchase of Manweb electric of England and Southern Water as well as others, there were no further takeovers planned for the near future, with attention refocused upon getting value from the companies they own and preparing for the introduction of competition in 1998.
-- BP STAKE PRICING OVERSUBSCRIBED

According to officials at US investment bank Goldman Sachs, its placing of 170 million British Petroleum shares, one of the biggest-ever sales of blocks of shares, was "comfortably oversubscribed". Goldman Sachs had acquired the shares from the Kuwait Investment Office. Shares were offered at 716p each and BP representatives were pleased with the "muted" reaction of the stock market to the GS placement.
-- MAID SEEKING SOFTWARE FACE

UK business information vendor Maid has expressed a desire to make a move into the software industry by transforming itself into a fully-fledged software company. Maid, which produces InfoSort, a program allowing computer users to search databases for information, would enter the search software market, in a collaboration with Digital Equipment and is in talks with IBM subsidiary Lotus. On Thursday, Maid released its 1997 first quarter figures showing an operating loss of 1.21 million sterling and pre-tax profits of 2.35 million with turnover of 6.75 million sterling, up from 4.48 million sterling.
-- "GOLDEN SHARE" WORRY FOR BT MERGER

With approval from the European Commission for their 20 billion dollar merger, British Telecom and MCI, collectively known as Concert, now have one remaining obstacle to overcome before the completion of their deal: the US Federal Communications Commission. There is some worry within the two groups that the FCC may oppose the merger due to the UK government's holding of a "golden share" in BT which gives it power to veto any potential buyers allowing them rights within Concert that the US government could not equal. It is possible that the FCC would only approve the deal if the "golden share" is relinquished, but BT officials doubt that will be the case.
-- BG UPSTREAM SIDE SHOWS RECOVERY SIGN

British Gas has released the first-quarter results for its upstream operations, showing operating profits at 40 million sterling, a production rise of 50 percent, pre-tax profits up to 615 million sterling and turnover up 12 million sterling to 1.14 billion sterling. Cost-saving measures the company had introduced were offset by costs of preparing for competition in the domestic gas market. BG called the results encouraging, adding that production profile should rise over the next few years and that the negative impact of warmer weather should only cost 83 million sterling.
